Additionally, the presence of a shared lowest common ancestor—Tricyclic Antidepressant—underscores a broader pharmacological context in which Imipramine and its analogs interact with Cyp1a2. While the direct causal link between Imipramine and Cyp1a2 remains indirect, the evidence supports a plausible mechanism involving the pharmacological interaction of related compounds. The integration of these pathways suggests that Imipramine may contribute to Cyp1a2 regulation through a mechanism that involves shared molecular features and pharmacological effects.
